summary.text: A crystal system is a set of point groups, which are groups of geometric symmetries that leave at least one point fixed.
Crystals can be classified three ways, by lattice system, crystal system or crystal family, and these terms are often confused with one another.
In three dimensions there are 7 crystal systems, 7 lattice systems and 6 crystal families, with the trigonal and hexagonal systems combined into one family.

items.prompt: Two crystals turn out to have very similar symmetries. As a rough rule, what would you expect about their classification?

options.label: They probably share one crystal system
They must have identical chemistry
They must be different crystal systems
They will always be the same colour

items.explain: Informally, crystals with similar symmetries are in the same crystal system, though there are many exceptions.

items.prompt: A student's report refers to a 'trigonal lattice'. What is wrong with that term?

options.label: Trigonal lattices exist only in four dimensions
Trigonal names a crystal system, not a lattice system
Trigonal is an old name for the cubic lattice
Trigonal lattices were dropped as too rare

items.explain: There is no trigonal lattice system; the trigonal crystal system is often confused with the rhombohedral lattice system, so the term is avoided.

items.prompt: Seven lattice systems times four kinds of centering gives 28 combinations, yet there are only 14 Bravais lattices. Why?

options.label: Half have never been seen in a real mineral
Centering works only in two dimensions
Face-centering is allowed only for cubes
Some repeat others and some break symmetry

items.explain: Some combinations are equivalent to other lattices, and others are impossible for symmetry reasons, leaving 14 unique ones.

items.prompt: You add extra lattice points to just one pair of opposite faces of a cubic cell. What do you get?

options.label: A cubic lattice with a larger cell
A new, fifteenth Bravais lattice
A tetragonal lattice, no longer cubic
A hexagonal lattice with six sides

items.explain: Centering only one pair of faces removes the threefold rotation axes that define the cubic system, leaving a body-centered tetragonal lattice.

items.prompt: For a flat, two-dimensional pattern, how do crystal families, crystal systems and lattice systems relate?

options.label: All three groupings coincide
Lattice systems do not exist in 2D
Systems outnumber families, as in 3D
Families outnumber the other two

items.explain: In two-dimensional space the crystal families, crystal systems and lattice systems are the same.

items.prompt: Going from three-dimensional to four-dimensional space, what happens to the number of crystal systems?

options.label: It stays at 7
It climbs to 33
It drops to 4
It becomes infinite

items.explain: Three-dimensional space has 7 crystal systems, while four-dimensional space has 33.
